nodes.name: Server movement intent
nodes.purpose: Player movement intent for the NetQuake server: friction, ground and air acceleration, swimming, and view pitch helpers.

nodes.name: Server physics
nodes.purpose: Entity integration and clipping for the NetQuake server: gravity, velocity limits, stair walking, wall friction, and projectile tossing.

nodes.name: World collision

nodes.name: QuakeWorld player move
nodes.purpose: Client-side player movement and collision for QuakeWorld: friction, acceleration, jumping, swimming, and hull tests.

nodes.purpose: QuakeWorld weapon fire routines and projectile launch values for hitscan, rockets, nails, lightning, and grenades.

cards.name: Ground acceleration and friction
cards.summary: Ground movement reaches a fixed top speed quickly, then friction pulls the player to a stop.
cards.behavior: The intended direction comes from the yaw of the view angles. The server caps the requested horizontal speed, measures the shortfall along that direction, and adds acceleration proportional to the requested speed, limited by the shortfall. Friction lowers speed each frame and uses a stop-speed floor, so slow motion decays gently. Near a ledge the friction coefficient doubles, which prevents accidental slides off edges.

constants.name: Maximum ground speed
constants.unit: map units/second of intended ground speed, applied per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Ground acceleration
constants.unit: acceleration coefficient per second, applied per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Ground friction
constants.unit: friction coefficient per second, applied per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Stop speed
constants.unit: map units/second of speed floor for friction, applied per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Edge friction multiplier
constants.unit: friction multiplier applied near a ledge, evaluated per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

cards.name: Air control
cards.summary: Airborne steering has a small speed ceiling, so jumps keep most of their momentum.
cards.behavior: When no floor contact exists, ground friction is skipped and steering acceleration uses a separate low cap on desired speed. The player can change direction in the air, but the change accumulates slowly because only a small amount of velocity is added along the new direction. Existing horizontal momentum remains dominant for the whole jump.

constants.name: Air steering speed cap
constants.unit: map units/second of desired air speed, applied per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Air acceleration coefficient
constants.unit: acceleration coefficient per second, applied per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Air speed clamp reference
constants.unit: map units/second of normal ground speed, used per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

cards.name: Jump impulse
cards.summary: Jumping adds a fixed upward velocity only from the ground and only after the jump key is released.
cards.behavior: The jump input is edge-triggered. A grounded player receives a fixed upward impulse, and the jump flag stays set until the key is released, which prevents automatic bunny hopping from a held key. In deep water the normal jump is replaced by a small upward swim speed. Facing a low ledge while swimming triggers a separate exit move with a stronger upward push and a forward burst.

constants.name: Jump velocity
constants.unit: map units/second of upward velocity, applied per movement command, command rate unverified

constants.name: Water exit upward velocity
constants.unit: map units/second of upward velocity, applied per movement command, command rate unverified

constants.name: Water exit forward velocity
constants.unit: map units/second of forward velocity, applied per movement command, command rate unverified

constants.name: Water swim upward velocity
constants.unit: map units/second of upward velocity, applied per movement command, command rate unverified

cards.name: Water movement
cards.summary: Deep water reduces top speed, adds vertical intent, and makes idle players sink slowly.
cards.behavior: At waist depth or deeper the movement mode becomes swimming. Horizontal intent is combined with vertical intent, and zero input produces a slow downward drift. The desired speed is capped and then reduced by a swim factor. Drag lowers all three velocity components each frame, so direction changes feel heavy and momentum fades quickly.

constants.name: Swimming depth tier
constants.unit: water depth tier, evaluated per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Idle sink rate
constants.unit: map units/second of downward drift, applied per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Swim speed factor
constants.unit: multiplier of the normal ground speed cap, applied per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Water friction
constants.unit: drag coefficient per second, applied per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

cards.name: Stair stepping
cards.summary: The player climbs low steps by lifting, moving forward, and dropping onto the higher floor.
cards.behavior: A normal slide move is attempted first. When it blocks on a rise, the player is lifted by the step height, moved forward at the original horizontal velocity, and dropped. A landing surface must be flat enough to count as ground, or the move reverts to the unstepped result. If progress stalls, the server nudges the player in several directions and retries the move.

constants.name: Step height
constants.unit: map units of vertical step reach, applied per walking move at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Ground normal threshold
constants.unit: surface normal Z component threshold, evaluated per landing at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Unstick probe duration
constants.unit: seconds per recovery move, applied per unstick attempt at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Unstick side step
constants.unit: map units of lateral nudge, applied per unstick attempt at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

cards.name: Gravity and velocity clamp
cards.summary: Falling speed grows linearly with gravity and is capped per axis before each move.
cards.behavior: Every server frame adds downward acceleration scaled by the entity gravity multiplier. Before integration, each velocity axis is clamped to a maximum positive and negative value, so boosts and falls cannot exceed the engine limit. There is no quadratic air drag, which means fall speed grows at a constant rate until the clamp or a floor stops it.

constants.name: Gravity
constants.unit: map units/second squared, integrated per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Maximum velocity per axis
constants.unit: map units/second, clamped per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Default entity gravity multiplier
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier, applied per server frame at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

cards.name: Bouncing projectiles
cards.summary: Tossed objects reflect from surfaces with extra restitution and settle when vertical speed is low.
cards.behavior: Toss-mode entities integrate velocity and gravity, then clip against the first surface. A bounce reflects the velocity with extra restitution, so each impact loses less speed than a pure mirror. On a floor-like surface, low vertical speed or a non-bouncing mode clears both linear and angular velocity, which makes the object come to rest.

constants.name: Bounce reflection multiplier
constants.unit: velocity multiplier per surface impact, evaluated per bounce at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Settle speed
constants.unit: map units/second of vertical speed, checked per landing at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

constants.name: Floor normal threshold
constants.unit: surface normal Z component threshold, evaluated per landing at the dedicated default of 20 Hz

cards.name: View bob
cards.summary: The first-person eye height cycles with horizontal speed and is clamped against extreme offsets.
cards.behavior: View height follows a sine-like cycle whose amplitude is proportional to horizontal speed. The cycle has a configurable period and an upward fraction, which makes the rise faster than the fall. The final offset is clamped, and standing still removes the effect because speed drives the amplitude.

constants.name: Bob amplitude scale
constants.unit: view units per map unit/second of horizontal speed, applied per client frame, rate unverified

constants.name: Bob cycle period
constants.unit: seconds per full cycle, evaluated per client frame, rate unverified

constants.name: Bob upward fraction
constants.unit: fraction of the cycle used for upward motion, applied per client frame, rate unverified

constants.name: Bob upper clamp
constants.unit: view units of maximum upward offset, clamped per client frame, rate unverified

constants.name: Bob lower clamp
constants.unit: view units of maximum downward offset, clamped per client frame, rate unverified

cards.name: View roll and damage kick
cards.summary: Side speed rolls the camera, and damage adds a short pitch and roll kick.
cards.behavior: Lateral velocity rolls the view around the forward axis, strongest at high side speed and limited to a small angle. Damage adds a temporary pitch and roll kick whose size follows the damage amount and hit side, then decays over the kick time. Both effects combine with the base view angles.

constants.name: Maximum view roll
constants.unit: degrees at full lateral speed, applied per client frame, rate unverified

constants.name: Full roll speed
constants.unit: map units/second of lateral speed, evaluated per client frame, rate unverified

constants.name: Kick decay time
constants.unit: seconds of decay, applied per damage event

constants.name: Damage roll kick
constants.unit: degrees at full kick strength, applied per damage event

constants.name: Damage pitch kick
constants.unit: degrees at full kick strength, applied per damage event

cards.name: Mouse look
cards.summary: Mouse counts become view angles through sensitivity and separate yaw and pitch scales.
cards.behavior: Raw mouse counts are scaled by sensitivity, then converted to yaw and pitch by separate degree-per-count values. Pitch is clamped so the view cannot flip past vertical, and roll is clamped separately. Keyboard turning adds a constant angular rate while a key is held, and a speed key raises that rate.

constants.name: Mouse sensitivity
constants.unit: multiplier per mouse count, applied per input sample, rate unverified

constants.name: Yaw per mouse count
constants.unit: degrees per mouse count, applied per input sample, rate unverified

constants.name: Pitch per mouse count
constants.unit: degrees per mouse count, applied per input sample, rate unverified

constants.name: Upper pitch limit
constants.unit: degrees, clamped per client frame, rate unverified

constants.name: Lower pitch limit
constants.unit: degrees, clamped per client frame, rate unverified

cards.name: Third-person camera
cards.summary: A chase view pulls the camera back and up while aiming at the point the player looks at.
cards.behavior: The third-person view starts from the first-person eye point, moves backward along the view direction, shifts right and upward by the configured offsets, then aims at the point the player is looking at. There is no obstacle sweep, so geometry can block the view. The offset values are exposed as user settings.

constants.name: Chase distance
constants.unit: map units behind the player, applied per client frame, rate unverified

constants.name: Chase height
constants.unit: map units above the player, applied per client frame, rate unverified

constants.name: Chase side offset
constants.unit: map units to the player right, applied per client frame, rate unverified

cards.name: Shotgun pellets
cards.summary: One shell fires six hitscan pellets inside a small square spread.
cards.behavior: Each pellet traces to the first solid surface within a long fixed range and applies its own small damage. Hits on one target are summed into a single damage event, so a close blast is far stronger than a distant one. The spread is small enough that most pellets hit a nearby target.

constants.name: Pellet count
constants.unit: pellets per shot

constants.name: Damage per pellet
constants.unit: health points per pellet, applied per shot

constants.name: Square spread radius
constants.unit: fraction of forward distance, applied per pellet per shot

constants.name: Pellet range
constants.unit: map units, applied per pellet per shot

cards.name: Super shotgun pellets
cards.summary: The super shotgun spends two shells for fourteen pellets in a wide, flat pattern.
cards.behavior: The super shotgun spends two shells to fire fourteen pellets. Horizontal spread is much wider than vertical spread, so the pattern covers a broad cone at close range and loses effectiveness at distance. A single remaining shell falls back to the normal shotgun.

constants.name: Pellet count
constants.unit: pellets per shot

constants.name: Horizontal spread radius
constants.unit: fraction of forward distance, applied per pellet per shot

constants.name: Vertical spread radius
constants.unit: fraction of forward distance, applied per pellet per shot

cards.name: Rocket ballistics
cards.summary: Rockets fly straight at high speed, deal direct damage, and add a strong blast.
cards.behavior: Rockets travel in a straight line at high speed and expire after a fixed lifetime. A direct hit deals a base amount plus a small random bonus. The blast adds distance-scaled splash damage to other targets, excluding the direct victim.

constants.name: Direct damage
constants.unit: health points per direct hit

constants.name: Direct damage bonus
constants.unit: health points of random direct bonus, applied per hit

constants.name: Splash damage
constants.unit: health points at the blast center, applied per explosion

constants.name: Rocket speed
constants.unit: map units/second of projectile speed, applied per launch

constants.name: Rocket lifetime
constants.unit: seconds of game time, applied per rocket

cards.name: Nailgun ballistics
cards.summary: Nails are fast small projectiles with a short refire delay and two damage tiers.
cards.behavior: Nails are fast, small projectiles with a short refire delay. The normal nail deals light damage, while the super nail costs two rounds and deals double damage. Both use the same launch speed and expire after several seconds.

constants.name: Nail damage
constants.unit: health points per nail, applied per hit

constants.name: Super nail damage
constants.unit: health points per super nail, applied per hit

constants.name: Nail speed
constants.unit: map units/second of projectile speed, applied per launch

constants.name: Nail refire delay
constants.unit: seconds between shots, applied per nailgun shot

cards.name: Lightning beam
cards.summary: The lightning gun traces a short beam that damages targets along its path.
cards.behavior: The lightning gun traces a beam to the first solid surface within its fixed range and damages valid targets along the beam path. Each shot spends one cell. Firing under deep water discharges all remaining cells in a radial blast instead of producing a beam.

constants.name: Beam damage
constants.unit: health points per strike, applied per shot

constants.name: Beam range
constants.unit: map units of reach, applied per shot

constants.name: Underwater discharge damage
constants.unit: health points per cell, applied per underwater shot

cards.name: Grenade ballistics
cards.summary: Grenades arc at moderate speed, bounce, and explode on a fixed fuse.
cards.behavior: Grenades launch at moderate speed with an upward arc and bounce off surfaces. A fixed fuse detonates them, and the explosion applies distance-scaled splash damage. Because the fuse runs on game time, a long throw can detonate away from the aim point or after the target has moved.

constants.name: Grenade launch speed
constants.unit: map units/second, applied per throw

constants.name: Grenade upward arc
constants.unit: map units/second of upward velocity, applied per throw

constants.name: Grenade fuse
constants.unit: seconds of game time, applied per grenade

constants.name: Grenade splash damage
constants.unit: health points at the blast center, applied per explosion

cards.name: Damage knockback
cards.summary: Damage pushes walking targets away from the blast and splash falls off with distance.
cards.behavior: Damage to a walking target pushes it along the direction from the blast center at eight speed units per health point. Quad damage multiplies incoming damage before both health loss and push. Splash damage falls off linearly with distance, self-damage is halved, and the search radius exceeds the nominal blast by a margin.

constants.name: Knockback per damage
constants.unit: map units/second of push per health point, applied per damage event

constants.name: Quad damage multiplier
constants.unit: damage multiplier, applied per powered hit

constants.name: Self-damage multiplier
constants.unit: damage multiplier, applied per self-inflicted blast

constants.name: Blast search margin
constants.unit: map units added to blast radius, applied per explosion

cards.name: Player collision hull
cards.summary: The player collides as a square box with an asymmetric vertical span.
cards.behavior: The player uses an axis-aligned box for collision, with a square footprint and an asymmetric vertical span. The origin sits inside the box, so the eye point must be offset upward. Movement resolves against this box rather than a capsule, which shapes stair and ledge behavior.

constants.name: Hull minimum X and Y
constants.unit: map units, applied per collision test, rate unverified

constants.name: Hull minimum Z
constants.unit: map units, applied per collision test, rate unverified

constants.name: Hull maximum X and Y
constants.unit: map units, applied per collision test, rate unverified

constants.name: Hull maximum Z
constants.unit: map units, applied per collision test, rate unverified

cards.name: First-person eye height
cards.summary: The first-person camera sits a fixed height above the player origin.
cards.behavior: The default eye point sits a fixed height above the player origin. The view code adds this height before applying bob and pitch. Changing the eye height changes perceived scale without changing the collision box.

constants.name: Default eye height
constants.unit: map units above the player origin, applied per client frame, rate unverified

cards.name: Input speeds and run modifier
cards.summary: Keyboard movement uses fixed speeds, and a speed key doubles them and raises turn rates.
cards.behavior: Keyboard movement builds forward, side, and vertical intent from fixed speeds. Holding the speed key doubles all three intent values. Keyboard turning adds yaw and pitch at fixed angular rates, and the same speed key raises the turn rate.

constants.name: Forward speed
constants.unit: map units/second of intended movement, applied per input sample, rate unverified

constants.name: Side speed
constants.unit: map units/second of intended movement, applied per input sample, rate unverified

constants.name: Speed key multiplier
constants.unit: movement multiplier, applied per input sample, rate unverified

constants.name: Keyboard yaw rate
constants.unit: degrees/second, applied per client frame, rate unverified

constants.name: Keyboard pitch rate
constants.unit: degrees/second, applied per client frame, rate unverified

constants.name: Speed key angle multiplier
constants.unit: angular rate multiplier, applied per client frame, rate unverified

cards.name: Swept box collision
cards.summary: Movement sweeps a box through the BSP world and stops at the first blocking surface.
cards.behavior: A move test selects a hull that matches the entity size, sweeps the box from start to end, and returns the first blocking plane, the impacted entity, and the fraction of the path that was clear. Solid entities are linked into the world so nearby triggers and other solids can find them. Moving links also dispatch touch events when a solid overlaps another entity.
